name: Anteromedial approach to the talus
corridor: Incision from the medial malleolus toward the navicular, protecting the saphenous vein and nerve and staying off the posteromedial deltoid arterial branches to the talar body

positioning.text: Position so the medial malleolus, navicular, and medial neck can be seen; this window is usually combined with an anterolateral approach.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the medial malleolus, navicular, and the saphenous vein and nerve.

incision.text: Incise from the medial malleolus distally to the navicular. For more complex fractures, especially if a medial malleolar osteotomy is planned, extend more inferiorly and proximally.

superficial_interval.text: Identify the long saphenous vein and nerve. Vein branches may be ligated or coagulated. Stay immediately medial to the tibialis-anterior sheath if the distal-tibia anteromedial interval is used as the proximal guide.

deep_interval.text: Evacuate hematoma to see the inferomedial neck. Do not damage the deltoid arterial branches that arise posteromedially and supply the medial two-thirds of the talar body. Minimize periosteal stripping.

layers.text: Skin, saphenous vein and nerve, then the medial talar neck with preserved deltoid arterial branches.

structures_at_risk.text: The saphenous nerve and vein, the deltoid arterial branches to the medial talar body, and remaining extraosseous talar vessels after a fracture-dislocation are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Posteromedial stripping of deltoid branches and broad periosteal elevation of the neck are the osteonecrosis danger zones.

retraction_hazards.text: Do not retract posteromedially into the deltoid arterial leash or strip periosteum off the neck to improve the view.

exposure.text: Shows the medial neck for reduction and medially based fixation. Combined with the anterolateral window it is used for displaced and comminuted neck fractures.

limitations.text: Does not show the lateral neck or subtalar joint. A more inferior proximal cut is needed if a medial malleolar osteotomy is added for the medial talar dome.

indications.text: Used with an anterolateral approach for displaced or comminuted talar-neck fractures so the medial reduction and medial fixation can be seen.

complications.text: Complications include saphenous neurapraxia and talar osteonecrosis from injury to deltoid branches or periosteal stripping.

procedure_applications.condition: The medial talar neck is reduced and fixed, usually together with an anterolateral window; the cut is shifted more inferior proximally if a medial malleolar osteotomy is planned

questions.question: From where to where does the anteromedial talar incision run?
questions.answer: From the medial malleolus distally to the navicular, extended more inferiorly and proximally if a medial malleolar osteotomy is planned.

questions.question: Which arterial branches must be preserved on the medial side?
questions.answer: The deltoid branches that arise posteromedially and supply the medial two-thirds of the talar body.

questions.question: Why is this approach usually combined with an anterolateral window?
questions.answer: Displaced and comminuted neck fractures need both sides seen for an anatomic reduction.
